issues: No tel: call link

[reviewer] No phone number is rendered anywhere and there are zero tel: links; topbar 'Call for today's hours' (index.html:28), hero-meta (index.html:59-61), and Visit 'call us for today's hours' (index.html:122) are dead text. A brake shop's #1 conversion tool is the phone. Fix: show the shop's actual number in the topbar and Visit/address and wrap each in href="tel:+1...", and point the 'Request a Callback' banner (index.html:112) at it too. This also resolves the structural gate finding.

[reviewer] All five service cards (index.html:73-78) plus the strip, hero visual, and about card reuse the identical wrench glyph — the icon loads as one visual, not five services. Fix: give each card a distinct on-message SVG (brake disc/rotor, check-engine gauge, oil drop, gearbox, clipboard-check) so a scan reads the offering at a glance.

[reviewer] Hero h1 (styles.css:128, index.html:51) crams the full 35-char business name plus a second accent headline in clamp-up-to-4.6rem Archivo Black; at 360px it stacks into ~5 tall lines and buries the offer. Fix: shorten the display line (e.g., 'Bothell Import Service' with a small 'auto repair' kicker), keep 'Honest repairs, clear pricing' as a tight one-liner, and set a mobile-safe clamp floor around 2.3rem.

[reviewer] All three reviews (index.html:102) cite anonymous '— Google review' with no reviewer name or context, so the 4.1/56 social proof reads as template filler. Fix: use the real reviewer names (or initials + date) from the Google aggregate so the quotes carry concrete credibility.

[reviewer] Visit section (index.html:122) punts 'Hours vary by day — call us for today's hours' with no number behind it — evasive rather than specific. Fix: publish the seven-day hours table in the Visit card (it's the one concrete fact locals look for), or replace the placeholder with a real call prompt tied to issue #1.

praise: Copy is genuinely specific, not adjective-stuffed: real street address, 4.1/56 Google rating, named services (Brakes & Rotors, Check-Engine, Oil & Maintenance, Engine & Transmission), and the 'Diagnostics before dollars' promise — no lorem, no 'welcome to our website'.
The deep-navy / burnt-orange / gold palette is disciplined and carried through hero, cards, CTA banner, stats, and even the scrollbar — it reads as a brand for this shop, not generic gradient soup.
Hero hierarchy lands: badge → business name → single one-line offer → one clear CTA, with heavy motion safely gated behind prefers-reduced-motion and a no-JS fallback.
Mobile base holds together: nav collapses at 760px with a proper toggle, stats/visit/about grids stack, and clamp() type scale plus full-width .btn-call give reasonable 360px tap targets.

praise: Copy is genuinely specific and human — street address, 'Diagnostics before dollars' hook, same-day/no-upsell review quotes, dealer-level scans — zero lorem or welcome-filler, and the diag-first narrative threads badge, tagline, checklist, and services as one message.
Palette stays disciplined: deep navy frame with a single warm orange/gold accent family; gradients are used in a few high-signal places (hero accent, primary button) instead of gradient soup.
Typography pairing (Archivo Black display / Archivo body) is purposeful, with a confident clamp() scale, tight display letter-spacing, and ~60-70ch body columns.

Motion is tasteful and correctly gated: magnetic CTAs, reveal/word-mask entrances, aurora canvas, count-ups and parallax all respect prefers-reduced-motion and pointer:fine — the design would still hold up fully static.
